newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Energy Dept to discuss SPR use with industry.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Energy Dept to discuss SPR use with industry.

text.p: U.S. Energy Department officials plan to ask oil industry executives Friday how the Strategic Petroleum Reserve could be used to help ease a potential shortage of heating oil, a senior energy official said Thursday.
Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary is set to meet 15 chief executives from oil and gas companies Friday afternoon to discuss heating oil supplies.
"We'll talk about the SPR -- when they think it might be appropriate to use it," said Associate Deputy Energy Secretary Kyle Simpson.
Simpson said at the meeting the department would explain some of the proposals it had received, mainly from Northeastern lawmakers, on how to shore up heating oil supplies or fend off a price jump.
"Right now, most of the suggestions would require a declaration of an emergency. And at this time, no emergency exists," Simpson said in a brief interview.
Proposals that called for the government to buy distillate for storage would be counterproductive, he said. "In a market that's already tight, it would probably tighten the market."
The Energy Information Administration Thursday reported that heating oil stocks on the East Coast last week were 43 percent, or 18 million barrels, lower than a year ago.

Ever since consumer group Citizen Action and Northeastern lawmakers raised concern about the depleted stocks last month, Energy Department officials have repeatedly said they did not intend to get into the heating oil market.
Energy Department officials and analysts are not expecting any major market announcements after the meeting Friday.
"Hopefully, we'll have more of an understanding of how the industry's going to deal with this," Simpson said.
While lawmakers did not expect immediate action out of Friday's meeting, "we do expect the ball to be rolling," said one Congressional aide.
